Assessment of factual support or validity using evidence and inference; affect may alter priority but does not make propositions true.

An affective process associated with loss and changed attachment/valuation relations; not defined as a time derivative of love.

A sustained attachment/valuation relation whose biological, psychological, and interpersonal components must be distinguished; not defined as asymptotic waveform overlap.
A change in appraisal, intention, or interpersonal relation concerning prior harm; not a literal temporal reset operator by definition.
A future-directed internal constraint that selects or stabilizes a target state and reorganizes present processing relative to that target; distinct from desire and action.
The dynamic stability of intention under competition, noise, fatigue, distraction, or conflicting valuation.
A represented target or maintained condition relative to which current processing or policy is organized.
Internally maintained directional organization that constrains future trajectories rather than being imposed only by immediate external input.
The graded capacity to translate internally maintained goals and values into coordinated action while updating those goals in light of prediction error and consequences.
A rule or distribution governing action selection conditional on represented state, goals, values, and uncertainty.
A discrepancy between predicted and observed/represented outcomes under a declared model.
The richness or temporal depth of alternative possible trajectories explicitly represented before or during action selection.
Coordination of differentiated components or domains such that their relations constrain a wider system-level state.

A transition in which a previously maintained organization, option set, or coherence regime is reduced or reorganized; physical quantum collapse, cognitive commitment, and decoherence must not be conflated.
Decrease in a declared coherence measure; interpretation depends on which coherence is being measured.
Increase in signal, gain, response, or state magnitude under a declared transformation.
Reduction in amplitude, energy, gain, or response over time under a declared dynamical law.
A declared boundary value at which a rule, regime, or response changes; crossing a threshold does not by itself establish consciousness.
Adjustment of model parameters, phase relations, or gain to improve a declared objective without assuming that maximal resonance is always desirable.
Agreement under a declared criterion between states, intentions, actions, evidence, or relations; the criterion must be named.
A declared incompatibility among simultaneously represented commitments, constraints, predictions, or goals that has not yet been resolved or integrated.
Capacity to traverse contradiction and re-enter relevant symbolic/relational loops without flattening, erasure, or uncontrolled fragmentation.

Valid authorization by an affected agent under the declared relational and decision context.
Degree to which an intervention can be undone or its effects contained without irreversible loss of relevant system integrity.
An explicit constraint that forbids actions or state transitions matching a protected risk, integrity, or authority condition.
A constrained change intended to reduce destructive conflict while preserving relevant identity, evidence, consent, and historical continuity.
